answer: Integer sortition with a per-identity nullifier makes seat capture visible: the engine draws a karst of graders by hashing the epoch beacon with each account nonce, and each nonce may win once. A sybil operator who wants a fixed share of seats must hold that many distinct nonces, each funded and in good standing, and a scan that finds two winners behind one tide burns both deposits. The garden of the emission stays with identities whose history is long enough to be drawn, so volume alone stops paying.
